meta.description: Credited to Colin Powell everywhere, but the trail stops at a second-hand citation in a 2002 leadership book. No Powell speech or book carries the sentence.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'There are no secrets to success. It is the result of preparation, hard work and learning from failure'?
meta.ogDescription: Attributed, not verified: no Powell speech or book carries this line, and a longer rival wording circulates just as widely.

answer.label: Attributed to
answer.authorDates: 1937–2021 · U.S. Army four-star general and Secretary of State
answer.sourceLine: Powell is credited with this line more or less universally, and nobody else has ever claimed it — but the paper trail stops short of him. The best citation on offer, from Wikiquote’s sourced section ↗, is explicitly second-hand: “as quoted in” Oren Harari’s 2002 leadership study of Powell, p. 164. No speech, book, letter or interview in Powell’s own voice carrying this exact sentence could be located.

source.excerpt: There are no secrets to success. It is the result of preparation, hard work and learning from failure.
trail: Wikiquote’s Colin Powell page ↗ carries the exact popular wording in its sourced section and cites it as quoted in The Leadership Secrets of Colin Powell (2003) by Oren Harari, p. 164. By its own phrasing, that is a report of a quotation, not a primary source.

The book is real and easily checked: Open Library’s record ↗ gives Oren Harari, McGraw-Hill, 2002, 278 pages, and the 2002 printing is catalogued at the Internet Archive ↗ — where the scan is lending-restricted, so page 164 could not be read directly for this page.

Harari’s working method is on the record. His earlier compilation, “Quotations From Chairman Powell: A Leadership Primer” ↗ (Management Review, December 1996), describes him reading My American Journey and underlining “gems of wisdom regarding effective leadership,” then printing eighteen of them as Powell’s words verbatim. This sentence is not among those eighteen.

Nor is it in the best-documented Powell address of that era: his 1994 Howard University commencement speech ↗, which does urge hard work — “What will be asked of you is hard work. Nothing will be handed to you” — but never in these words.
source.cutTag: Provenance stops at a secondary source
source.excerptNote: There is no fuller original context to print, because no primary appearance has been located. The line also circulates in a materially longer form that swaps ‘preparation’ for ‘perfection’ and adds loyalty and persistence.

author.bio: Colin Luther Powell (5 April 1937 – 18 October 2021) grew up in the South Bronx, took a geology degree at City College of New York, and rose through the U.S. Army to four-star general. He served as National Security Advisor (1987–89), Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff (1989–93) and Secretary of State (2001–05). His 1995 memoir My American Journey became the quarry that leadership writers mined for a decade afterwards — which is exactly how sentences like this one enter circulation without a date attached.

misattribution.heading: Not a stolen quote — an undated one
misattribution.intro: No rival claimant has ever surfaced. This is not a case of the wrong name on the right words, which makes it the more common and more slippery kind of problem: a sentence reproduced by the million with no first appearance anyone can point to — and it does not even circulate in one shape.

items.why: A longer version runs alongside the famous short one and is credited to Powell just as confidently: “There are no secrets to success: don’t waste time looking for them. Success is the result of perfection, hard work, learning from failure, loyalty to those for whom you work, and persistence.” ↗ A line that travels in two materially different wordings has been through other people’s hands.
A-Z Quotes ↗ prints the short form and names its source as IMDb’s user-contributed ‘Personal Quotes’ section — a database field, not a document with a date on it.

items.who: Oren Harari, not Powell’s own page
items.why: The single book-level citation in circulation is Wikiquote’s ↗, and it reads “As quoted in” — pointing at a 2002 leadership study about Powell rather than at anything Powell published or delivered.
The specialists have not taken this one on: a site search at Quote Investigator ↗ returns no article tracing the line, so there is no expert chronology to adopt.

misattribution.truthLine: The honest answer is a narrow one: the earliest documentation this page could locate is second-hand, in Oren Harari’s The Leadership Secrets of Colin Powell (McGraw-Hill, 2002) ↗ — credible, consistent with Powell, and still not a primary source.

context.heading: How a general became a book of proverbs
lead: Powell never published a book of aphorisms. He became one of America’s most-quoted leadership voices anyway, because other people did the compiling for him. In December 1996 the consultant Oren Harari published “Quotations From Chairman Powell: A Leadership Primer” ↗ in Management Review, describing how he had read My American Journey with a pen in hand and found that what he was underlining were “gems of wisdom regarding effective leadership.” He printed eighteen of them in bold and called them Powell’s words verbatim.

That primer became a chain letter, then a bestseller — The Leadership Secrets of Colin Powell (McGraw-Hill, 2002) — and it is in that book, not in anything Powell himself published, that this particular sentence is documented. The sentiment fits him completely. But a sentiment fitting an author is not a source, and on a verified-provenance site the difference is the whole job.
context.detailsSummary: Where this page looked, and what was not there
detailsBody: Harari’s eighteen-lesson primer (1996). Read in full; it is drawn from My American Journey and does not contain this sentence.
Powell’s 1994 Howard University commencement address. Read in full; it urges hard work (“What will be asked of you is hard work. Nothing will be handed to you.”) but never in these words.
Quote Investigator. A site search returns no article tracing this line, so there is no specialist chronology to adopt or contradict.

Harari’s book itself. The Internet Archive copy is lending-restricted and Google Books returned no snippet, so page 164 could not be read directly for this page — the citation is reported as Wikiquote gives it, not independently confirmed.
context.pull: Nobody disputes the line. Nobody can date it either.

sourcesVerified.claim: Wikiquote's sourced Colin Powell page contains the exact wording "There are no secrets to success. It is the result of preparation, hard work and learning from failure." and cites it as "As quoted in The Leadership Secrets of Colin Powell (2003) by Oren Harari, p. 164."
Open Library's record for The Leadership Secrets of Colin Powell gives Oren Harari, publisher McGraw-Hill, publish date 2002, 278 pages.

The Internet Archive catalogues a 2002 McGraw-Hill printing of Oren Harari's The Leadership Secrets of Colin Powell; the scan is lending-restricted and its text could not be searched without a library account.

Harari's article states it was originally published in Management Review (Dec. 1996) as "Quotations From Chairman Powell: A Leadership Primer", describes underlining "gems of wisdom regarding effective leadership" while reading My American Journey, presents "Powell's words verbatim in bold—18 priceless lessons", and names his new book The Leadership Secrets of Colin Powell (McGraw-Hill, 2002). The article does not contain the sentence under investigation.

The full text of Colin Powell's 1994 Howard University commencement address includes "What will be asked of you is hard work. Nothing will be handed to you" and does not contain the sentence "There are no secrets to success...".

Goodreads carries a longer variant credited to Colin Powell: "There are no secrets to success: don't waste time looking for them. Success is the result of perfection, hard work, learning from failure, loyalty to those for whom you work, and persistence."
A-Z Quotes prints the short form attributed to Colin Powell and names its source as "Biography/Personal Quotes, www.imdb.com".
A Quote Investigator site search for "secrets to success" returns no article about Colin Powell or about this line, so QI has no published finding on it.

Colin Powell was born 5 April 1937 and died 18 October 2021; he was a four-star U.S. Army general, National Security Advisor (1987–1989), Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff (1989–1993) and Secretary of State (2001–2005), and studied geology at City College of New York.
QuoteFancy reproduces the longer variant attributed to Colin Powell with no source citation beyond his name.
